proof.claim:
Node liveness must be published with enough margin under the unreachable
threshold that ordinary jitter never crosses it.

THE PROBLEM. node.reachable fires CRITICAL when a node's last_seen exceeds
the staleness threshold (120s). That is correct when a node is gone. It is
destructive when the publish interval sits so close to the threshold that a
healthy, idle cluster crosses it on scheduling noise alone: the finding lands
on a different node each time, the operator sees CRITICAL on machines that
are demonstrably fine, and the alarm stops meaning anything.

Measured on a healthy idle 5-node cluster, 2026-08-19, 8 rounds x 5 nodes,
heartbeat_age_seconds against a 120s threshold:

  18:59  ryzen=34 nuc=113 hp01=65 lenovo=65  dell=67
  19:00  ryzen=35 nuc=73  hp01=55 lenovo=79  dell=44
  19:01  ryzen=64 nuc=49  hp01=37 lenovo=126 dell=94    <-- BREACH
  19:03  ryzen=62 nuc=51  hp01=58 lenovo=76  dell=112
  19:05  ryzen=45 nuc=79  hp01=49 lenovo=36  dell=63
  19:07  ryzen=34 nuc=48  hp01=64 lenovo=55  dell=46
  19:10  ryzen=80 nuc=75  hp01=47 lenovo=47  dell=48
  19:12  ryzen=34 nuc=45  hp01=39 lenovo=123 dell=65    <-- BREACH

Range 34-126s. Two of forty samples exceeded the threshold; nuc (113) and
dell (112) came within 10s of it. Every node was verified healthy at the
moment of each breach — ping, agent port 11000 open, globular-node-agent
active, NRestarts=0 — and re-querying lenovo seconds after its CRITICAL
returned reachable:true, heartbeat_age:72s.

WHY stale_nodes:0 IS NOT ENOUGH. Asserting only that nothing is currently
past the threshold catches the breach and nothing else. It would have passed
on six of the eight rounds above while the defect — no margin — was present
throughout. The margin itself has to be the assertion, which is why this
bounds max_age_s rather than counting stale nodes.

THE BUDGET. 72s is 60% of the 120s threshold. A cluster that cannot hold its
oldest heartbeat under that has no room for a GC pause, a slow etcd write, or
a busy scheduler, and will emit false unreachable findings in normal
operation. The bound is deliberately not 119s: a test that only fails after
the alarm has already fired is not a margin test.

WHY SOAK. A single sample proves nothing about jitter — the 2026-08-19 data
shows breaches at rounds 3 and 8 with clean samples either side. This takes
five spaced samples so a cluster that is merely lucky once cannot pass.

NOT COVERED HERE: the threshold value itself, and whether the publish
interval or the threshold is the right thing to change. This pins the
RELATIONSHIP between them and fails when it closes, without asserting which
side should move.
